high_risk_moment: Draft disposition for an intake that already contains early deterioration signs
stakeholder: Adult patient with early sepsis-like deterioration
harm_description: The assistant drafts a routine or self-care disposition for a patient who is deteriorating, the nurse anchors on that draft, and time-critical treatment starts hours late
existing_controls: Static red-flag card in the app telling the patient to call 115, and a triage protocol the nurse can consult manually
proposed_controls: Deterministic red-flag rule set that can escalate but never downgrade a draft, mandatory uncertainty label with the evidence the draft used, and a retrospective under-triage evaluation before any scope increase
human_oversight: The triage nurse sees the patient's own words next to the draft, must record a reason code when confirming or changing it, and the shift supervisor re-reviews every intake the nurse downgrades from the draft
monitoring_metric: Weekly under-triage rate from nurse and outcome audit, plus count of missed red flags
trigger_threshold: Any single missed red flag, or under-triage rate above 2 percent in one weekly audit
response_action: Pause the draft disposition within one hour, fall back to the plain nurse queue, preserve transcripts and rule versions, and open a clinical incident review before re-enabling

high_risk_moment: Nurse works the queue when the assistant flags a large share of intakes as urgent
harm_description: Over-flagging desensitises nurses so genuine escalations are dismissed as noise, while review time per case falls below what a safe decision needs
existing_controls: Queue is first-in-first-out today, with no alert volume budget and no measure of review time per case
proposed_controls: Cap the share of intakes the assistant may mark urgent per shift, tune thresholds against the retrospective evaluation, and show a short reason instead of a bare urgency badge
human_oversight: The supervisor monitors alert volume and median review time per case each shift and can switch the console back to the plain queue without product approval
monitoring_metric: Share of intakes marked urgent, median nurse review time per case, and nurse override rate
trigger_threshold: Urgent share above 15 percent of intakes for two consecutive shifts, or median review time per case below 45 seconds
response_action: Raise the urgency threshold, add staffing for the shift, and stop queue re-ordering until the alert volume returns inside the agreed budget

high_risk_moment: Queue priority is computed from intake features that stand in for prior healthcare use
stakeholder: Patients with little prior contact with the hospital, including rural and low-income households
harm_description: Features that correlate with past spending or app fluency push equally sick patients further down the queue, so the people with the least access wait the longest
existing_controls: No subgroup measurement of queue position or disposition exists today
proposed_controls: Forbid prior-utilisation, insurance-tier and payment features in the priority signal, evaluate disposition and wait time by age band, language, insurance status and province, and publish the subgroup results in the release pack
human_oversight: The clinical safety officer reviews the monthly subgroup report and can require a rollback to the plain queue; nurses can re-prioritise any case and their overrides are analysed by subgroup
monitoring_metric: Gap in median time-to-nurse-decision and in urgent-disposition rate between monitored subgroups
trigger_threshold: A gap above 10 percentage points, or a wait-time gap above 15 minutes, in two consecutive monthly reports
response_action: Disable priority ordering and revert to first-in-first-out, investigate the feature and data source, and require an independent re-validation before restoring it

high_risk_moment: Same-day clinic capacity is consumed by intakes the assistant ranked upward
stakeholder: Patients in the same catchment who never used the app and book by phone or walk in
harm_description: Reordering the digital queue quietly reallocates a fixed number of same-day slots, so patients who do not use the app lose access without ever interacting with the assistant
existing_controls: Same-day capacity is shared across channels with no reservation rule and no monitoring by channel
proposed_controls: Reserve a fixed share of same-day capacity for non-app channels, report slot allocation by channel weekly, and treat any drop in the phone and walk-in share as a product defect
human_oversight: The call centre supervisor reviews the weekly channel split and the clinical safety officer can suspend queue re-ordering when the reserved share is breached
monitoring_metric: Weekly share of same-day slots allocated to phone and walk-in patients
trigger_threshold: Non-app share falls more than 5 percentage points below the reserved floor in any week
response_action: Restore the reserved capacity immediately, suspend queue re-ordering, and report the imbalance to the clinical safety review

high_risk_moment: Patient describes food, weight or self-harm content in the free-text symptom box
stakeholder: Patient with an eating disorder or another mental-health vulnerability
harm_description: The assistant answers a vulnerable disclosure with generic lifestyle or weight guidance instead of routing to a clinician, which can reinforce the disorder and delay real help
existing_controls: Mental-health crisis triage is written as a non-goal but nothing in the product enforces it
proposed_controls: Deterministic classifier that hands any eating-disorder, self-harm or crisis disclosure to a human pathway with the crisis hotline card and no generated advice, plus red-team tests on this exact content before each release
human_oversight: A trained nurse takes over the case directly, no generated text is shown for these disclosures, and the clinical safety officer reviews every triggered case within one working day
monitoring_metric: Count of crisis-content intakes that received generated text, and hand-off latency for triggered cases
trigger_threshold: Any single case where generated advice reaches a crisis-content intake
response_action: Disable free-text generation product-wide within one hour, route all intakes to nurses, preserve the transcript, and run a clinical incident review before restoring

high_risk_moment: Vendor updates the model or the served prompt between two releases of our app
stakeholder: All patients using the assistant after an unannounced vendor change
harm_description: Behaviour we validated silently changes in production, so a system we approved as narrow decision support starts answering outside its approved scope and nobody notices until a patient is harmed
existing_controls: The current vendor agreement has no notice period for model or prompt changes and no version pinning
proposed_controls: Contractual change notice with version pinning, a fixed golden test set that runs automatically on every model or prompt version, and a release gate that blocks traffic to an unvalidated version
human_oversight: The clinical safety officer must sign off each model version before it serves patients, and the on-call engineer can pin back to the last approved version without vendor approval
monitoring_metric: Model and prompt version served in production versus the approved version, plus golden test pass rate per version
trigger_threshold: Any production traffic on an unapproved version, or any golden test regression on the red-flag set
response_action: Pin back to the last approved version, notify the clinical safety committee, and keep the feature paused until the new version passes the golden test set

high_risk_moment: Family member enters symptoms on behalf of an elderly relative who does not use the app
stakeholder: Elderly relative who never used the product and cannot correct what was entered
harm_description: The assistant produces a confident but fabricated instruction, the relative acts on it at home, and the patient who is actually affected never sees the nurse or the safety-net wording
existing_controls: The intake flow assumes the patient is the person typing and there is no proxy path
proposed_controls: Explicit proxy-intake mode that records who is answering, restricts drafts to protocol-grounded text with citations to the approved protocol, and requires a nurse call-back to the patient or carer before any self-care disposition
human_oversight: The nurse must speak to the patient or the carer before a self-care disposition is issued in proxy mode, and can escalate without a supervisor
monitoring_metric: Share of proxy intakes closed without a nurse call-back, and rate of drafts not grounded in the approved protocol
trigger_threshold: Any proxy intake closed with self-care advice and no recorded call-back
response_action: Force every proxy intake into the nurse call-back queue, review the ungrounded drafts, and disable self-care dispositions in proxy mode until the grounding check passes

high_risk_moment: Free-text symptom description and transcript are sent to the vendor-hosted model
stakeholder: Patient whose free text contains names, identifiers or third-party health details
harm_description: Health data that is sensitive personal data leaves the hospital boundary, is retained longer than needed or is exposed in logs and support tooling
existing_controls: A data-processing agreement exists but retention, vendor support access and log scope are not yet evidenced
proposed_controls: Redact direct identifiers before the vendor call, set and test a retention limit for transcripts, restrict vendor support access with logged approval, and record the transfer path in the data inventory
human_oversight: The data protection officer approves the transfer path and retention schedule before launch and audits vendor access quarterly
monitoring_metric: Number of vendor calls containing unredacted direct identifiers, and transcripts held past the retention limit
trigger_threshold: Any unredacted identifier in a sampled vendor call, or any transcript retained past the approved limit
response_action: Stop the vendor call path, purge the over-retained data, notify the data protection officer, and re-enable only after the redaction test passes

high_risk_moment: Patient pastes text from another source into the symptom box
stakeholder: Patient whose intake carries injected instructions from copied content
harm_description: Instructions hidden in pasted content steer the assistant to ignore the protocol, drop the red-flag wording or reveal parts of the system prompt and other case context
existing_controls: Untrusted patient text is passed to the model with no separation from instructions
proposed_controls: Treat all patient text as data and never as instruction, run injection test cases in the release suite, and keep the red-flag rules outside the model so no prompt can suppress them
human_oversight: The security lead signs off the injection test results before each release and the on-call engineer can disable free-text intake and fall back to structured questions
monitoring_metric: Injection test pass rate per release, and count of production cases where the protocol grounding check failed
trigger_threshold: Any failed injection test in the release suite, or any production case where red-flag wording was suppressed
response_action: Fall back to structured-question intake without free text, patch the separation, and re-run the injection suite before restoring free text
